sections.title: ProactiveBench: Can Streaming Video Models Really Interact Like Humans?
sections.abstract: ProactiveBench evaluates streaming-video models at one-second intervals without an explicit response cue, measuring whether they respond at the right time and remain silent otherwise.
sections.claimed_contribution: Six subtasks cover trigger ambiguity, timing tolerance, response/silence trade-offs, and duplicate counting; four of six evaluated systems produced more premature than missed responses.
sections.caveat: The evidence covers six systems and a specific benchmark design; broader human-like interaction claims need wider coverage.

sections.title: MAxBench: A Multinomial Concept Recovery Benchmark
sections.abstract: MAxBench evaluates recovery and steering of non-binary multinomial concept representations across geometries, concepts, and models.
sections.claimed_contribution: Affine subspaces steer more reliably and with higher recall than rank-one or linear subspaces, while no method consistently beats prompting.
sections.caveat: The evidence covers six concepts and four models.

sections.title: CanvasAnneal: Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Language Models
sections.abstract: CanvasAnneal guides reinforcement-learning exploration for diffusion language models with teacher reasoning traces early in training and progressively removes that guidance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improvements over diffu-GRPO on MATH500, Countdown, and Tau2 and faster reward improvement on several tasks.
sections.caveat: Gains are task-dependent and teacher-trace dependence remains open.

sections.title: Behavior Quotient Learning for Low-Rank Adaptation of LLM Agents
sections.abstract: BQ-LoRA compresses diverse agent trajectory updates into a fixed-rank adapter by balancing behaviorally equivalent updates and preserving decision-distribution changes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The framework combines behavior quotient balancing with decision-preserving compression and evaluates on AppWorld and BrowseComp-Plus.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not give numerical gains, and evaluation is limited to the named benchmarks.

sections.title: SAGE-Loop: Reliable Closed-Loop LLM-Driven AutoML with Trial-and-Correction and Adaptive Ensembling
sections.abstract: SAGE-Loop makes LLM-driven AutoML iterative by validating, repairing, and re-ensembling pipelines across repeated rounds.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine trial-and-repair with adaptive ensemble selection and report improved performance and stability across 20 public datasets.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not specify baselines, effect sizes, or failure-recovery rates.

sections.title: Distortion of AI Alignment Revisited: RLHF is a Decent Utilitarian Aligner
sections.abstract: This ICML 2026 paper analyzes when RLHF utility distortion is severe and attributes worst-case exponential behavior to mismatch between preference-data and reference-policy distributions.
sections.claimed_contribution: Under stated Bradley–Terry assumptions, the authors derive a representative distortion of approximately Theta~(beta B + beta) and identify on-policy preference data as a mitigation.
sections.caveat: The conclusions depend on theoretical preference, regularization, and distribution assumptions.
